Celo: MiniPay integrates Link by Stripe for one-click stablecoin purchases - 12 Nov 2026 Less than 1 min read

CELOUSD MiniPay's Link by Stripe integration is scheduled for 12 Nov 2026. Users in the EU and US can buy stablecoins in one click, then save, spend and send them on Celo. The integration adds a fiat onramp to MiniPay's existing base of more than 20 million wallets. It gives those users a direct route from fiat money to stablecoins for payments on Celo, supporting payment activity and visibility for the CELO token.

News / London Stock Exchange / REG - KR1 PLC - Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations

REG - KR1 PLC - Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations Refinitiv 3 min read

KR1 RNS Number : 7982C KR1 PLC 12 November 2026   KR1 plc Thursday, 12 November 2026 KR1 plc (“KR1” or the “Company”) Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations KR1 plc KR1 , a London Stock Exchange-listed onchain infrastructure company, is pleased to provide an update on its Venice (“VVV”) operations. Following its October Infrastructure Income & Holdings update, in which it reported holding 276,223 VVV valued at £5.77 million as at 30 September 2026, the Company has fully staked its current holding of 275,000 VVV, earning rewards in VVV at an indicative annualised staking rate of approximately 5.74% as at 11 November 2026. Based on available disclosures, the Company believes it is the largest publicly listed holder of VVV, with approximately 0.56% of the circulating supply, a position that reflects its conviction in the convergence of AI and crypto. Venice is a core holding within KR1’s Technology Infrastructure Strategy. In its Introducing Decentralised AI announcement on 14 May 2026, the Company disclosed an initial holding of 60,000 VVV and the commencement of staking operations. KR1 has since increased its position. Founded by renowned crypto entrepreneur Erik Voorhees, Venice provides access to frontier and open-source AI models for generating text, code, images, video and audio. The platform is designed around privacy, model choice and user control. Venice’s adoption continues to accelerate. Its October community update reported 5 million users, with the increase from 4 million taking 68 days. Daily inference volume exceeded one trillion tokens during October, compared with approximately 250 billion at the end of September. On 14 October, Venice’s Erik Voorhees reported annual revenue exceeding US$150 million. In July, Venice also announced a US$65 million Series A led by Dragonfly, at a stated US$1 billion valuation, to expand its consumer platform and API business. KR1 puts its Venice assets to productive use in two ways. First, the Company stakes VVV to generate infrastructure income in the form of newly issued VVV tokens. Reward rates vary, and standard VVV unstaking is subject to a seven-day cooldown. The second route uses DIEM, a token that holders can mint by locking staked VVV. KR1 acquired its DIEM separately and stakes it to access daily credits for AI inference on Venice. KR1 makes that inference capacity available to customers through third-party marketplaces. Venice’s buy-and-burn programme creates a further connection between commercial adoption and VVV. The platform allocates 5% of API credit purchases to buying VVV on the open market and permanently removing it from supply. New Pro, Pro+ and Max subscriptions trigger purchases and burns of US$2, US$5 and US$10, respectively, alongside discretionary burns. Venice reported that the value of VVV burned during October had exceeded US$1 million by 28 October. Revenue-funded purchases create demand for VVV, while burns reduce VVV supply relative to continuing issuance. This mechanism is separate from staking rewards and does not constitute a cash distribution to token holders. Keld van Schreven, Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc, commented: “We believe the convergence of AI and crypto could be one of the defining technology themes of the next decade. We put that conviction to work through our Venice operations, staking VVV to earn infrastructure income while retaining exposure to the platform’s growth. We can use those rewards to fund operations or reinvest them in productive assets. That reinvestment drives the KR1 flywheel, helping grow the earning capacity behind each KR1 equity share.” About KR1 plc KR1 plc owns and operates productive digital assets across the networks powering the convergence of AI and crypto. As the only dedicated onchain infrastructure company listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, KR1 draws on a decade of domain expertise to take a high-conviction, thesis-driven approach to its holdings, targeting a dual return profile: infrastructure income and capital appreciation. item.title: Asian markets mixed as Nvidia shares tumble; South Korea, Taiwan stocks slip
item.description: In the chip supply chain, SK Hynix slid, while Samsung Electronics surrendered part of its early gains. Traders also seemed to be watching Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) closely, since ...
item.content:encoded:
News / CNBC TV18 /

Asian markets mixed as Nvidia shares tumble; South Korea, Taiwan stocks slip NVDA NI225 KOSPI IX0001 Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday November 12, with little conviction as investors seemed to weigh the fresh turmoil at Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of this year's artificial intelligence rally. Japan's Topix gained 0.51% and the Nikkei 225 added 0.17%. South Korea's Kospi slipped 0.068%, and Taiwan's TAIEX lost 0.24%, while Hang Seng futures dropped 0.7%. In the chip supply chain, SK Hynix slid, while Samsung Electronics surrendered part of its early gains. Traders also seemed to be watching Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) closely, since any lasting damage to confidence in Nvidia could hit its key suppliers hardest. In India, the GIFT Nifty pointed to a muted start for the domestic market, though with a positive bias. The Nifty and the Nifty Bank both showed their first signs of exhaustion at higher levels after several sessions of strong gains, which suggested that the market could enter a phase of consolidation before it resumes its uptrend. The Nifty Bank was particularly in focus for the day's trade having come within 400 points of its previous record high. Separately, MSCI announced the results of its November review early Thursday. It added four Indian stocks to its Global Standard Index: Life Insurance Corporation of India, Coforge, Adani Green Energy and Meesho. Currency market in Asia too remains in focus as Japan's top currency official, Atsushi Mimura, told reporters according to a Bloomberg report that the Japanese yen's recent slide had been "too fast", adding that "It's too early to forget what happened this summer." The yen hovered near 160 per dollar, the level at which Tokyo stepped in over the summer. The trigger for the movement in Asian equities today, came in late US trading as Nvidia shares tumbled about 9% after Bloomberg reported that the company's board was meeting to discuss the future of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. Bloomberg said Huang had admitted to an affair with a woman whom US officials reportedly suspect of being a Chinese spy. The New York Times separately reported that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's healthcare vice president, citing several current and former employees. The shock cut short a strong day for US technology stocks, when the Nasdaq 100 had climbed 2.3%. Futures reversed course afterwards as Nasdaq 100 contracts fell more than 1%, and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.5%. Server makers Super Micro Computer and Dell Technologies also declined. Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom rose as traders seemed to have speculated that they could pick up business if Nvidia stumbled. CoreWeave had surged 25% on an upbeat outlook before giving back some of that gain. In energy markets, Brent crude remained steady at about $92.46 a barrel in early Asia trade, after two straight days of losses. A senior Iranian official rejected the idea of surrendering enriched uranium, which signalled that peace talks between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.
